cards.text: Paul, an apostle, is writing to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2), and he's just finished a whole chapter on love (1 Corinthians 13). Now he keeps rolling. Earnestly pursue love, he says, and eagerly desire spiritual gifts.

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians to eagerly desire spiritual gifts. Which gift does he single out?

cards.text: First up, speaking in a tongue: Paul says that person speaks to God, not to men, and no one understands him. He utters mysteries in the Spirit.

cards.question: Paul says that, unlike the one who speaks in a tongue, the one who prophesies speaks to people.

cards.text: Paul says prophecy is for edification, encouragement and comfort. Friend, that gift shows up like a whole care package.

cards.question: Paul says the one who speaks in a tongue edifies ___, but the one who prophesies edifies the church.

cards.text: Now hold on, Paul's not tossing tongues out of the kitchen. He says he wishes ALL of them could speak in tongues, but he'd rather have them prophesy.

cards.question: Paul says the one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, with one exception. What is it?

answers.text: Unless the whole church joins in

cards.text: Then Paul makes it personal: if he came to them speaking in tongues, how would that help them, unless he brought some revelation, knowledge, prophecy or teaching? Friend, if I showed up in your kitchen speaking only Stamper, you'd smile, nod, and QUIETLY go look up a recipe.

So Paul pulls out some everyday examples, starting with lifeless instruments like the flute and the harp. I spent YEARS as a lifeless tool in a junk drawer, friend, so I'm taking that word personally.

cards.question: Paul says a flute or a harp needs ___ notes, or no one will recognize the tune.
Paul's next example is a trumpet. He says even a muffled trumpet call gets everyone ready for battle.
A blurry flute and a muffled trumpet. What's Paul's point for the Corinthians?

answers.text: Their words must be understood to help

cards.text: Paul says there are many different languages in the world, and none of them is without meaning. Even the noises my oven makes mean SOMETHING, friend, I just haven't cracked the code yet.

cards.question: Paul says if he doesn't know the meaning of someone's language, he is a ___ to the speaker, and the speaker is one to him.
The Corinthians are eager to have spiritual gifts. Which gifts does Paul tell them to strive to excel in?

answers.text: The gifts that build up the church
The gifts that are hardest to get

cards.text: Next, Paul says the one who speaks in a tongue should pray that he may interpret. Here's why: when Paul prays in a tongue, his spirit prays, but his mind is unfruitful.

cards.question: When Paul prays in a tongue, his spirit prays, but his mind is unfruitful. So what does Paul say he will do?

answers.text: Pray with his spirit and his mind
Pray only with his mind from now on

cards.question: When it comes to singing, Paul says he'll sing with his spirit and leave his mind out of it.

cards.text: Now picture someone uninstructed sitting in the room while you speak a blessing in spirit and give thanks.

cards.question: Someone speaks a blessing in spirit. How can the uninstructed person say ___ to it, when he doesn't know what was said?

cards.text: Paul says you may be giving thanks well enough, but the other person isn't built up. It's like getting added to a group text where everybody's saying THANK YOU SO MUCH, and you heart it anyway with NO idea what for.

cards.question: Paul has been putting prophecy ahead of tongues, but he also says he speaks in tongues more than all of the Corinthians.
Even so, in the church, what would Paul rather speak than ten thousand words in a tongue?

answers.text: Five clear words that instruct others

cards.text: FIVE words beat TEN THOUSAND, friend, and that's every work meeting that should've been an email. Then Paul says it straight: “Brothers, stop thinking like children.”

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians to stop thinking like children. He says that in regard to ___ they should be infants, but in their thinking they should be mature.

cards.text: Then Paul quotes the Law (Isaiah 28:11-12), where the Lord speaks: “By strange tongues and foreign lips I will speak to this people, but even then they will not listen to Me, says the Lord.”

cards.question: Paul quotes the Lord speaking by strange tongues to people who still won't listen. Then Paul says tongues are a sign for believers, not for unbelievers.

cards.text: Prophecy, Paul says, is for believers. Now he paints a picture where the whole church comes together, everyone speaks in tongues, and in walk some uninstructed people or unbelievers.

cards.question: The whole church is speaking in tongues when visitors walk in. What does Paul say they'll say?

answers.text: That you are out of your minds
That you are just showing off
That you are a holy people

cards.text: But flip it: everyone's prophesying, and an unbeliever or uninstructed person walks in. Paul says he'll be convicted and called to account by all, and the secrets of his heart will be made known.

cards.question: The visitor is convicted and the secrets of his heart are made known. What does Paul say the visitor will do?

answers.text: He will fall facedown and worship God
He will walk out without a word
He will ask someone to interpret

cards.text: And Paul says he'll proclaim, “God is truly among you!” That's where we'll set the dough down for now, friend, because Paul is NOT done teaching this church yet.
